title: Voice Anti-Spoofing & Audio Watermarking — ASVspoof 5, AudioSeal, WaveVerify
service: Provenance: a toy spectral spoof detector, a SQLite audit log of detection decisions, AudioSeal-style watermark localization, live spoof alarms and C2PA-style manifest chains

parts.lesson_anchor: Build It, Step 1: a simple spectral-feature detector (toy); code/main.py magnitude_spectrum and toy_detector_score; quiz Q11 (framing off-by-one, slow DFT)
planted_bugs: frame_starts is the lesson's range(0, len - n_fft, n_fft), which never starts the last full frame; a one-frame clip gets no frames and the ZeroDivisionError surfaces one call up, in average_spectrum
power_spectrum returns the magnitude (the lesson's sqrt) although its docstring promises power, so the energy share becomes a magnitude share: -4.77 dB instead of -6.99 dB
high_band takes the FFT size to be len(spec), the number of one-sided bins (129), so the 4 kHz cutoff lands near 2 kHz and a 3 kHz tone counts as high band
toy_detector_score adds 1e-12 to both energies to keep away from log(0), so silence scores 1e-12 / 1e-12 = 0 dB, the most suspicious score, instead of FLOOR_DB
average_spectrum loops over bins outside frames, recomputing every frame's DFT for each of the 129 bins
parts.timing_assert: an 8-frame clip scored under 0.1 s (the per-bin recomputation takes 1.05-1.2 s, one DFT per frame 7.8-9.5 ms)
parts.overfix_guard: a copy 80 dB quieter scores the same (special-casing silence and keeping the constant on both energies shifts it); the score is clipped at the floor (a constant added to the share gives -99.49 dB); a trailing partial frame is dropped (range(0, n, n_fft)); a 4 kHz tone at the cutoff counts (n_fft = 2 * len(spec) puts bin 64 at 3969 Hz)

parts.lesson_anchor: Build It, Step 4: every generation ships a retention-policy-compliant audit log; Pitfalls: detection without calibration (calibrate on your domain); outputs/skill-spoof-defender.md audit log retention
parts.exactness: a threshold from a calibration sweep (0.1 + 0.2) and a score of 0.3 just below it round-trip exactly across close and reopen, so every verdict can be re-derived; times come back in UTC with their microseconds

deviations: Part 1: the three suggested defects (bin to Hz, the high-band energy normalization, log(0)) are joined by the lesson's own framing off-by-one (quiz Q11a), which gives the failure one call away from its cause; it drops the last full frame, the opposite of 06/03's partial frame. The normalization defect is the lesson's own too: its toy_detector_score sums magnitudes |X| and calls the result an energy share. The score is in dB with a floor. log(0) is planted as the usual guard against it, a constant added to both energies, which scores silence at 0 dB and makes quiet clips score differently; a bare log10(0) crash on silence would repeat 06/11's dBFS meter. The timing defect is a per-bin comprehension that recomputes every frame's DFT, because requiring an FFT would not fit ten minutes.

Part 2: times come back in UTC, the audit-log convention, instead of keeping the caller's offset as 06/08's consent registry does. The domain's precision trap is a calibrated threshold (0.1 + 0.2) with a score just below it, plus NaN, which SQLite stores as NULL. flips() adds the recalibration question from the lesson's calibration pitfall; the verdict is derived by the log, never passed in.

Part 3: per-sample probabilities stand in for the AudioSeal detector, so the part is the post-processing (strict threshold, bridge short gaps, then drop short segments, the order pyannote's Binarize uses) plus IoU against the ground truth. No payload is decoded, because 06/08 covers bit voting.

Part 4: the input is a stream of (t, score) batches from an upstream countermeasure model rather than audio, so 06/03's windowing of audio across chunks is not repeated. Smoothing is an exponential average in stream time with a half-life, so gaps in the score stream decay old evidence. The wire format is Server-Sent Events.

Part 5: the manifests carry no signatures; hashed ingredient references bind them. A loop raises ValueError before any hash check, because a hash-first walk can never follow a loop and would only report a mismatch. The origin is reported as the parentOf history, and AI involvement is looked for along both relationships.
